rationale: Product A projects the existing SequencerStateChannel as two typed, grantable control operations (dev.pulp.sequencer/state.read@1 and dev.pulp.sequencer/state.edit@1) bound to the HostMain executor, so Forge Sequencer and Forge Modular reach live pattern state through the unified control platform rather than through a CLI-only path. The diff adds the executor, its standalone-host channel seam, the two capability rows, the manifest operations and their JSON schemas, re-pins the control registry digest, and adds a dedicated Catch2 suite. One family is crossed by a test-registration file only: visual-proof-harness, via the test/cmake/view_widget_bridge_tests.cmake selector, because that manifest already owns every sibling control-executor test target and the new pulp-test-control-sequencer-state-executor target is registered alongside them. No screenshot, capture, golden, fixture, harness, threshold or visual-proof code is touched, and no import, DesignIR, renderer or asset surface is touched. Registered watch-only so the family's coverage stays honest about a change that crossed its selector. No authority moves and no Vellum artifact changes.
tests: sequencer state capabilities declare the HostMain executor binding
sequencer state read copies the published snapshot and playhead
sequencer state read honours explicit projection selectors
sequencer state edit submits one exact typed command
sequencer state edit encodes every declared edit kind
sequencer state edit refuses a malformed or out-of-range request
a full sequencer command FIFO is a typed retryable refusal and never a drop
both sequencer operations refuse an off-host-main-thread call
sequencer operations refuse an unresolvable or wrongly-tiered channel
sequencer operations refuse a foreign operation id and honour cancellation
